Everyone know about blood circulation. Well, you also have lymphatic circulation.

Here's the two systems, side by side: http://media.web.britannica.com/eb-media/16/161616-004-F97BD149.jpg

The (blood) circulatory system is closed. The lymphatic system is open. Lymph travels down, sort of bathes the tissues, mostly the fat tissues, and then is pumped back up and around.

A lot of things can damage the lymphatic system. Certain diseases can, mostly parasites. Occasionally, it just...gets damaged, usually as a side-effect from an autoimmune reaction where your body is trying to clear and infection and accidentally takes out part of you. But the most common cause is obesity. Almost everyone who is extremely obese has some level of lymphatic dysfunction.

This causes massive, massive swelling of the fat tissues, most often in the legs. It can be partially relieved by elevating the affected body part (but extremely obese people would smother to death) and lymphatic massage. But there is no outright cure. For many people, it's resolved with weight loss. That's how people on My 600 Pound Life can sometimes lose 70lbs in a month even though their TDEE is like 4500 calories and they're still eating 1500+ calories a day. Some of it really is "water weight"--or rather, horrific swelling in the limbs weight. They lose the fat that's clogging up the lymphatic system, it starts working better, the swelling goes down.

But for those whose systems are really, really damaged, weight loss doesn't do nearly enough. In this case, that is actually her THIGH, believe it or not, and even losing like 100lbs couldn't reverse the damage that had been done to it. Removal of the fat, in that case, reduces the accumulation (because lymph doesn't/can't hang out in muscle and bone). So she had that huge lump removed so she could walk. It would have gotten smaller with continued weight loss, but with the level of damage she'd done to her body, it was questionable whether she could ever walk again without the surgery.
